'''Boris Davison''' (7 October 1908 – 24 January 1961) was a Russian-born [[Mathematical physics|mathematical physicist]].

== Biography ==
Boris Borisovich Davison was born 7 October 1908 in [[Vasilsursk]], [[Gorky Oblast]], Russia.<ref name=":2">{{Cite book |last=Hager |first=Willi |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=6EF9BgAAQBAJ&dq=boris+davison+physicist&pg=PA1375 |title=Hydraulicians in Europe 1800-2000: Volume 2 |date=2014-03-21 |publisher=[[CRC Press]] |isbn=978-1-4665-5498-6 |pages=1375 |language=en}}</ref> He attended [[Leningrad State University]], graduating in 1931.<ref name=":3">{{Cite journal |last=Watson |first=W. H. |date=April 1961 |title=Prof. B. Davison |journal=[[Nature (journal)|Nature]] |language=en |volume=190 |issue=4773 |pages=306–307 |doi=10.1038/190306b0 |bibcode=1961Natur.190..306W |s2cid=4275244 |issn=0028-0836|doi-access=free }}</ref><ref name=":2" /> He then worked at the [[State Hydrological Institute]]. 

Davison's grandfather had been British, and in 1938 Davison was given a choice – either renounce his British nationality or leave the Soviet Union. He chose to emigrate to the United Kingdom.<ref name=":3" /><ref name=":2" /> He then briefly worked with [[Louis Rosenhead]] at the [[University of Liverpool]] but withdrew from work due to illness.<ref name=":2" /><ref name=":3" />  

In 1942 he joined the [[University of Birmingham]]'s atomic energy research team working under [[Rudolf Peierls]], and in 1944 the university awarded him a PhD.<ref name=":3" /><ref name=":2" /> 

In 1943 he moved to Canada to work under [[George Placzek]] at the [[Montreal Laboratory]] of the joint British-Canadian atomic energy project.<ref name=":3" /><ref name=":2" /><ref name=":4">{{Cite journal |date=1961-05-01 |title=Boris Davison |url=https://pubs.aip.org/physicstoday/article/14/5/76/422087/Boris-Davison |journal=[[Physics Today]] |language=en |volume=14 |issue=5 |page=76 |doi=10.1063/1.3057579 |issn=0031-9228|doi-access=free }}</ref> In October 1945 he briefly joined the [[British contribution to the Manhattan Project|British Mission]] at [[Los Alamos Laboratory]] in [[New Mexico]], part of the [[Manhattan Project]] which had just developed the [[Atom Bomb|atom bomb]].<ref name=":5">{{Cite book |last=Szasz |first=Ferenc Morton |url=http://link.springer.com/10.1007/978-1-349-12731-3 |title=British Scientists and the Manhattan Project |date=1992 |publisher=[[Palgrave Macmillan UK]] |isbn=978-1-349-12733-7 |location=London |page=134 |language=en |doi=10.1007/978-1-349-12731-3}}</ref> In 1946 Davison married Olga Hansen.<ref name=":1">{{Cite news |date=1961-01-28 |title=Boris Davison |pages=39 |work=[[Montreal Gazette|The Gazette]] |url=https://www.newspapers.com/image/420557712/ |via=[[Newspapers.com]]}}</ref> 

He worked at [[Chalk River Laboratory]] in [[Ontario]] before returning to the UK in 1947 to work at the [[Atomic Energy Research Establishment]] at [[Harwell, Oxfordshire|Harwell]], [[Oxfordshire]].<ref name=":3" /><ref name=":2" /> 

In 1953 his [[security clearance]] was revoked by the British government because his parents still lived in the Soviet Union, potentially putting Davison at risk of blackmail.<ref name=":0">{{Cite magazine |date=1953-09-07 |title=Positively Vet |language=en-US |magazine=[[Time (magazine)|Time]] |url=https://content.time.com/time/subscriber/article/0,33009,818804,00.html |access-date=2023-08-07 |issn=0040-781X}}</ref> He was given a year's [[leave of absence]] working at the University of Birmingham.<ref>{{Cite news |date=1953-08-26 |title=British A-Scientist Given Year's Leave |pages=1 |newspaper=[[The Washington Post]] |url=https://archive.org/details/per_washington-post_1953-08-26_28195}}</ref><ref name=":5" /> Davison then emigrated to Canada in 1954, where he took up a position at the computation centre at the [[University of Toronto]].<ref name=":4" /><ref name=":5" />

In 1957 he authored the book ''Neutron Transport Theory''.<ref name=":3" />

Davison died suddenly at his home in [[Toronto]] on 24 January 1961 at the age of 52.<ref name=":1" /><ref name=":3" /><ref>{{Cite news |date=1961-01-27 |title=Campus News Briefs |pages=2 |work=[[The Varsity (newspaper)|The Varsity]] |location=Toronto |url=https://archive.org/details/thevarsity80}}</ref>
